mechanism_claims.claim_text: Peptide 2 directly perturbs Gram-positive bacterial cytoplasmic membranes, supported by Sytox Green membrane-permeabilization assays in S. epidermidis ATCC 12228 and S. aureus ATCC 25923.
direct_assay_types: Sytox Green cytoplasmic membrane permeabilization assay
mechanism_claims.limitations: Representative fluorescence traces support membrane permeabilization kinetics; the exact plotted fluorescence values are not tabulated in local text.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Peptide 2 shows rapid bactericidal activity against S. aureus ATCC 25923 in CFU time-kill experiments at MIC-related concentrations.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=2.6:Killing Kinetics against S. aureus ATCC 25923; xml:fig=5:Figure 5

mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports bactericidal kinetics and mechanism context, not a specific molecular receptor target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Membrane-model assays support interaction with Gram-positive membrane mimics: zeta potential shifts, reduced membrane fluidity, and carboxyfluorescein leakage from POPG/POCL LUVs.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: peptides 1-3, with peptide 2 highlighted for leakage
mechanism_claims.limitations: LUV assays are membrane-model evidence and should not be overpromoted to an in-cell molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Structural CD/NMR evidence supports the authors' interpretation that Aib8 increases helical content and creates a bent/distorted helix associated with peptide 2 activity.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Structure-activity interpretation is source-backed but remains mechanistic context, not proof of a unique molecular target.
